title: QoS Handshake Stepper
description: MQTT offers three delivery promises. QoS 0 sends a PUBLISH once and never repeats it. QoS 1 repeats the PUBLISH until a PUBACK comes back, so the broker may process a repeat. QoS 2 uses a four-packet handshake (PUBLISH, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP) so the broker processes each packet number exactly once.

learningObjectives: The learner will infer, for 6 scenarios of a publisher sending one alert to a broker, how many copies of the alert the broker processes, with at least 5 of the 6 inferences right.
prerequisites: publisher, broker, QoS 0, QoS 1, QoS 2, PUBLISH, PUBACK, PUBREC, PUBREL, PUBCOMP, duplicate (all defined in the section "Delivery Promises" above this block).

keyQuestions: Does QoS 1 guarantee exactly one copy?
Does a lost acknowledgement mean the message was lost?
Why do alerts carry an id?
commonMisconceptions: (1) QoS 0 retries until the message gets through. (2) QoS 1 guarantees exactly one copy. (3) A lost acknowledgement means the message was lost. (4) QoS 2 never sends a packet twice.
assessmentOpportunities: Complete all six scenarios. Mastery is 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
